"Job gains have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined," but the Committee also notes that "overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent," and that market-based inflation compensation remains low. Interpreted through Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s rule-based New Keynesian framework, keeping the policy rate in a low target range while signaling “gradual increases” and a funds rate “below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run” is consistent with Taylor-type prescriptions when inflation is below target and labor markets are tight. Svensson and Woodford’s inflation-forecast-targeting perspective reinforces the emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent objective and on closely monitoring expectations, supporting the Committee’s cautious, data-dependent stance rather than a faster tightening. Operationally, the reliance on IOER and ON RRP to maintain the funds rate within the target range accords with Goodfriend’s (2002) discussion of modern operating frameworks, while the plan to begin balance sheet normalization “relatively soon” reflects a gradualist approach consistent with documented Fed interest-rate smoothing behavior. Taken together, the tone is moderately positive on growth and employment but tempered by softer inflation and subdued inflation compensation, warranting a slightly less positive sentiment than before.
